Strict concavity of F implies Q(h)=F'(h)(h+c)-F(h) decreases from c to -c, so the pentagon maximum is unique. G decreases, W increases, so the hexagon frequency strictly decreases. The independent standard-library numerical computation evaluates both angular integrals and direct edge-crossing Monte Carlo; finite checks are not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: This is a complete exact four-type IUR section classification for a canonical five-vertex three-dimensional polytope and every positive aspect ratio. It explains how the rare six-gon type changes with shape and identifies a unique globally optimal pentagon frequency, not just a one-off numerical example. The width-weighted normalization and distinct two-parameter angular integrals are geometrically motivated and nontrivial, useful for stereological and combinatorial section benchmarks.
